text: jquery.json-viewer's json2html() renders any string value that matches isUrl() as a clickable `<a href="..." target="_blank">` link, but the generated anchor has no `rel="noopener"` / `rel="noreferrer"` attribute anywhere in the file. Since $.fn.jsonViewer defaults `withLinks: true` and is designed to render arbitrary/untrusted JSON (e.g. an API response) directly into the DOM via $(this).html(html), any URL-shaped string value in that JSON becomes a target=_blank link the viewing user can click, and the linked page gets an unprotected `window.opener` handle back to the host page (reverse tabnabbing / CWE-1022), letting it navigate the opener to a phishing page. This is a missing standard protection (rel=noopener/noreferrer on externally-controlled target=_blank links), not a data-flow bug -- confirmed by grepping the whole file for noopener/noreferrer/rel= and finding zero occurrences while target="_blank" appears exactly once.

text: The isUrl() helper in jquery.json-viewer.js uses the regex /^(https?:\/\/|ftps?:\/\/)?([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,}([a-z0-9-]+)?(:(\d{1,5}))?(\/([a-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%]+)?)?$/i against the attacker-influenced JSON value rendered by the plugin. The subpattern ([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,} nests an unbounded quantifier (the character class '+') inside a group that is itself repeated unbounded ({1,}, i.e. '+') — the canonical (x+)+ catastrophic-backtracking shape. Its last repetition also overlaps character-class-wise with the following optional ([a-z0-9-]+)? segment, so a crafted string such as many 'a.' pairs (e.g. 'a.'.repeat(30000)) followed by a character that forces the overall ^...$ match to fail can make the engine retry many different ways to split the run between the repeated group and the trailing optional segments, causing a severe slowdown (ReDoS) on the single-threaded JS engine that is rendering this JSON. Taint is confirmed end-to-end: the json2html(json, options) parameter (line 41, itself a FLOWS_TO self-loop / tainted source reached from the plugin's public entry $.fn.jsonViewer) flows via an explicit CpgCall FLOWS_TO edge from htmlEscape(json) (line 45) to isUrl(json) (line 47) and on to urlRegexp.test(string) (line 22), and that test call is reachable_from_entry=true with hop_distance=1.
